To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce a fast and accurate convolutional neural network for semantic segmentation of images under resource constraints, which is based on a novel efficient spatial pyramid convolution.

we propose a new convolutional network, ESPNet (Efficient Spatial Pyramid of Dilate Convolutions for semantic segmentation) which is 22 times as fast as state-of-the-art network, PSPNet, and 180 times as small, yet only 8% lower in category wise accuracy.

(i) we introduce ESP, a new convolutional block, which is more efficient in terms of memory, computation, and power than all existing blocks, and (ii) we show how ESP can be used to build a semantic segmentation network that is 180 times smaller and 22 times faster than the state-ofthe-art network, and is more efficient than all the current efficient networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (a) the introduction of ESP, a new convolutional building block for semantic segmentation, (b) the introduction of a fast and efficient network for semantic segmentation, ESPNet, and (c) the introduction of new metrics to measure efficiency in edge devices.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ESPNet is a fast, efficient, and accurate semantic segmentation network that can be deployed on edge devices.
ESPNet is the most efficient CNN architecture for semantic segmentation of images under memory and computation constraints.
ESPNet is a new state-of-the-art CNN architecture that achieves high efficiency and high accuracy on semantic segmentation of images.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we introduce a new convolutional block called efficient spatial pyramid ( ESP ) and show its effectiveness on semantic segmentation.

, we introduce a new convolutional block that can be easily plugged-in to any existing CNN architectures and we demonstrate that the new block can be used to build a semantic segmentation network that is efficient, fast and accurate.
ESPNet achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency for semantic segmentation on a wide range of edge devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design principles of ESP can be used to build efficient and fast semantic segmentation networks that are suitable for resource constrained environments.
the design of a fast and efficient network for semantic segmentation is not mutually exclusive with accuracy.
we demonstrate that it is possible to build efficient semantic segmentation networks that are fast, accurate, and can run on edge devices.
